Description of Assessment Instrument Students in the Data Analytics for Accounting and Auditing Certificate program are assessed on their data analytics skills via the course projects in MAC 511, MAC 512, MAC 518. The projects allow students to choose any accounting or auditing related problem that you are interested in. Students are then required to find a related dataset and perform data analytics according to the following process: 1) Define the accounting or auditing related question that can be answered by the data; 2) Master the data by downloading, validating, cleaning, and importing it to the analytics tools (if not excel); 3) Perform appropriate analysis approach to the data to find the answer of your question; 4) Address and refine results using appropriate visualizations; 5) Communicate your analysis process and results in a written report and an oral presentation. Description of Assessment Method (Rubric attached) The project reports as well as the oral presentations will be assessed by two independent assessors using a rubric that consisted of five criteria and three levels of expectation. The five criteria are: 1) Identify the questions; 2) Master the data; 3) Perform test plan; 4) Address and refine results; and 5) Communicate insights and track outcomes. The three levels of expectations were 1) Unsatisfactory, 2) Satisfactory, and 3) Exemplary.

What are the new courses and descriptions that will go into the course catalog?
FIN431- Financial Technologies: The financial services industries are changing with the emergence of financial technology (FinTech).
This course introduces to the most cutting edge FinTech topics, equip the students with an understanding of the major FinTech products in the market, and provide an overview of the underlying technologies.

Topics may include but are not limited to: blockchain and cryptocurrencies, smart contracting, digital payments, crowdfunding, robo-advising, artificial intelligence, machine learning, and cloud computing.
FIN412- Introduction to Financial Data Analytics: The vast proliferation of data and the increasing complexity of technology continue to transform the way financial markets and the finance industry operate and compete.
This course covers the foundations of finance and statistical methods, and how to perform data analysis in real world financial data using a modern statistical programming environment.
Topics may include but are not limited to: an introduction to Python programming language, the techniques how to evaluate the risk-reward trade off in modern portfolio theory, analyzing time series data, and developing algorithmic trading strategies.
Finally, a short introduction to machine learning applications concludes the course.
FIN433- Machine Learning for Finance: The objective of this course is to present fundamental techniques in machine learning for canonical modeling and decision frameworks in the rapidly changing financial technology industry.
Data-centric exercises in Python will be included to reinforce

6 theoretical concepts and demonstrate the application of machine learning technology to financial data analytics. That change allows us to reduce the total number of credits for HPE students to 120 which is the minimum number of credits required for graduation as stated in our university manual 8.21.10.
Undergraduate Curricular Requirement.

BS Nutrition and BS Dietetics students are required to take the four-credit course.
A Course Change Form has been submitted to change NFS 210 to a 1cr lab to be taken concurrently with the NFS 207 lecture.
We are making this change to increase instructional efficiency in the department.
The major requirements must be changed to reflect the change to NFS 207 (3) + NFS 210 (1).

These tracks are no longer necessary as CHE undergraduate students can receive minors in comparable subjects through established programs and new minors recently approved at URI.
Minors are better understood by potential employers and graduate programs and will be on students’ transcripts and diplomas, which is similar to how the Biology and Pharmaceutical Tracks were presented.

The coursework and knowledge gained using minors instead of degree tracks will be the same, but will also be more flexible for students. This will allow for more flexibility for students in their elective options and in pursuing the various minors CHE students might be interested in pursuing.
